request.brief: I am creating a brand for children's products.

audience.value: Children as users and adults as buyers

signals.range: From a 5% accent up to full color fields
signals.because: The positioning is unknown, and children's products do not all need to be colorful.

signals.range: One follows the bold-color convention, one departs from it, one builds on a narrative
signals.because: The brief does not say whether the product must compete on a crowded shelf.

directions.name: Building Blocks
directions.summary: Flat fields of tomato, blue and sunflower on cream, composed like stacked shapes.

secondary.evidence: 62% of chroma-weighted area lies in the warm arc.
Block Blue and Sunflower differ by 170 degrees.
Curator assigns this because several bold colors meet in large, simple shapes.
4 roles each hold at least 15% of area. Curator confirms the layout uses adjacent flat fields.

method.chroma: Holds relative chroma from the base, capped at 1.1 times the base C.
Holds relative chroma from the base, capped at 1.1 times the base C.
Holds the base C, capped below the sRGB limit at each L.

reasoning.claim: Soft Black reaches 9.78:1 on Sunflower and Bright Cream reaches 5.9:1 on Block Blue, so type stays legible on the color fields.
Three large color fields give packaging and web layouts a simple, repeatable structure.
Large simple shapes make the composition, and not any one hue, the recognizable part of the brand.

do: Compose in large flat shapes with clear edges.
Assign one field to each product line if the range needs separating.
avoid: Do not add gradients or soft shadows to the fields.
Do not place Tomato and Block Blue directly behind small text.

accessibility.standard: WCAG 2.2 contrast computed from sRGB HEX
notes: Contrast applies to the listed pairs only. Check any new pairing before use.
Do not rely on color alone for meaning. Pair state or status color with text, shape or an icon (WCAG 1.4.1).
Soft Black on Tomato is specified for large text only.

directions.name: Wood and Felt
directions.summary: Oat, walnut and stone with a pale peach, for products bought by design-minded parents.

secondary.evidence: 100% of chroma-weighted area lies in the warm arc.
All visibly hued colors fit a 30 degree arc.
100% of non-foundation chromatic area is pale and gentle.

method.chroma: Holds relative chroma from the base, capped at 1.1 times the base C.
Holds relative chroma from the base, capped at 1.1 times the base C.
Holds the base C, capped below the sRGB limit at each L.

reasoning.claim: Bark reaches 11.97:1 on Oat, so the soft palette remains comfortable to read.
A quiet palette lets the products and photography supply the color, which suits a range sold to parents on material quality.
Pale Peach occupies 5% of the declared area, keeping the direction within Neutral.

do: Let natural materials and product photography lead.
Use Pale Peach for small backgrounds and labels.
avoid: Do not use Pale Peach for text.
Do not choose this direction if the product must stand out on a crowded shelf.

accessibility.standard: WCAG 2.2 contrast computed from sRGB HEX
notes: Contrast applies to the listed pairs only. Check any new pairing before use.
Do not rely on color alone for meaning. Pair state or status color with text, shape or an icon (WCAG 1.4.1).
Pale Peach is decorative on Oat. Use Bark for any text placed on it.

directions.name: Nightlight
directions.summary: Deep indigo with a moon yellow, pink and mint, suited to bedtime and story products.

secondary.evidence: 64% of chroma-weighted area lies in the cool arc.
Story Night and Moon Yellow differ by 177 degrees.
Primary reaches 11.36:1 on the foundation and 100% of figure area reaches 4.5:1.
Curator assigns this because bright, candy-like figures sit against a storybook night ground.

method.chroma: Holds relative chroma from the base, capped at 1.1 times the base C.
Holds relative chroma from the base, capped at 1.1 times the base C.
Holds the base C, capped below the sRGB limit at each L.

reasoning.claim: Moon Yellow reaches 11.36:1 on Story Night, and Story Night labels read at the same ratio on Moon Yellow buttons.
A night-time scene gives the color a narrative reason, which suits bedtime or story products but not every children's range.
Pillow White carries reading text at 13.98:1.

do: Use Moon Yellow for the main character, mark and action.
Use Bubble Pink and Mint for small illustrated details.
avoid: Do not give pink and mint equal weight with Moon Yellow.
Do not use this direction for daytime or outdoor product ranges without testing it.

accessibility.standard: WCAG 2.2 contrast computed from sRGB HEX
notes: Contrast applies to the listed pairs only. Check any new pairing before use.
Do not rely on color alone for meaning. Pair state or status color with text, shape or an icon (WCAG 1.4.1).
